name: Pertisau
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village on the southern shore of the Achensee, with views of the Karwendel mountains and a lakeside dock.
beschreibung:
Overview

Pertisau is situated at an elevation of 952 metres on the southwestern shore of Lake Achensee, Tyrol's largest lake, in the district of Schwaz. Nestled on an expansive alluvial fan of mountain streams between the crystal-clear, fjord-like waters and the towering limestone walls of the Karwendel range, Pertisau forms the heritage-rich gateway to the Karwendel Nature Park. As part of the municipality of Eben am Achensee, the village is home to approximately 750 permanent residents. Pertisau benefits from exceptional peace and tranquility, as the lakeside road ends here in a cul-de-sac, completely eliminating through traffic. Right at the edge of the village, three celebrated valleys – Falzthurntal, Gerntal, and Tristenautal – open into the largest protected nature reserve of the Northern Limestone Alps. For centuries, Pertisau has combined summer retreat charm, sublime scenery, high-end wellness hotels, and first-rate outdoor pursuits across all four seasons.

History

Documented history in the Achen Valley dates back to 1112 with an extensive donation of land to the Benedictine monastery of St. Georgenberg-Fiecht. In the 15th century, the Tyrolean rulers recognized the scenic splendour of the site: Archduke Sigmund the Wealthy erected the first princely fishing lodge in 1466. Emperor Maximilian I and Archduke Ferdinand II subsequently established Pertisau as their beloved summer hunting retreat, organizing extravagant lake pageants; this royal lodge evolved into today's storied Hotel Fürstenhaus am Achensee. The launch of the steamship St. Josef in 1887 and the Achensee cog railway in 1889 ushered in modern tourism. An economic breakthrough occurred in 1902 when Martin Albrecht discovered oil shale in the Bächental, founding the production of genuine Tyrolean Shale Oil (Tiroler Steinöl). In 1934, the Golf- und Landclub Achensee was established as Tyrol's very first golf course. The striking modern Parish Church of the Holy Trinity was designed by master architect Clemens Holzmeister and consecrated in 1968.

Getting There

Reaching Pertisau is straightforward by road and rail alike. Motorists arriving via Austria or Italy take the Inntal Autobahn A12 to the Wiesing/Achensee exit, continuing along the B181 federal road past Maurach; from Germany, a scenic toll-free route runs from the A8 via Holzkirchen, Lake Tegernsee, and the Achenpass directly into the valley. Rail passengers arrive at Jenbach station, a major railway junction served by international ICE, Railjet, and Nightjet trains. From the forecourt in Jenbach, frequent VVT regional bus route 4111 runs straight to Pertisau centre and the Karwendel cable car. During summer, travellers can opt for a romantic nostalgic arrival: taking the historic steam cog railway from Jenbach up to Seespitz, followed by a scenic connecting cruise aboard the Achensee shipping fleet directly to Pertisau pier.

Tips

A premier cultural attraction is the Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg Visitor Centre, housed in a quartz-crystal-shaped glass pavilion featuring an underground mine gallery, interactive museum, and panoramic café. The Karwendel Cable Car carries hikers and paragliders up to the 1,491-metre Zwölferkopf, providing breathtaking aerial vistas of the turquoise lake alongside family ski slopes and a natural toboggan run in winter. Ambitious hikers should climb Mount Bärenkopf (2,089 m) for iconic alpine photography. Leisurely strolls, cycling tours, and horse-drawn carriage rides explore Falzthurntal towards the Gramai Alm or Gerntal towards the Gernalm. In addition to water sports and the historic 18-hole championship golf course, Pertisau transforms each winter into a world-class cross-country skiing hub with over 200 kilometres of groomed trails.
